fatal_errors: The proposed method omits the actual HPHT treatment at 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours, instead presenting the resulting coherent-interface feature as the intervention.
It does not identify the Al0.7CoCrFeNi FCC/B2 eutectic high-entropy alloy or its brittle, incoherent lamellar starting structure.

Deformation twinning is incorrectly treated as the main mechanism; the target mechanism centers on dislocation transfer across coherent FCC/B2 interfaces, stress-relief, and the combined activity of dislocations, stacking faults, microbands, and twins.
The cited evidence only establishes the general strength-ductility dilemma and provides no support for coherent nanoscale boundaries, HPHT processing, or the asserted mechanism.
The proposed experiment lacks a controlled comparison and interface, deformation, or fracture measurements capable of distinguishing the hypothesis from alternatives.
explanation: The hypothesis recognizes the broad strength-ductility problem and partially recovers one important structural feature—coherent internal interfaces—as well as twinning as one contributing deformation mode. However, it fails to reconstruct the processing method, material system, required pressure-temperature-time conditions, hierarchical microstructure, principal interphase dislocation-transfer mechanism, quantitative property gains, and pressure-dependent boundary conditions. Its predicted outcome and baseline are generic, while its evidence and falsification experiment do not substantiate or discriminate the claim.
